title: pipeline: wire GroupFilter into PipelineCtx + run_pipeline() group loop
description:
## What
Wire GroupFilter into PipelineCtx and apply group filtering in run_pipeline() before appending to the group log; update transit/main.rs startup to build GroupFilter from config and pass to pipeline.

## Algorithm
1. In crates/transit/src/peering/pipeline.rs, add field to PipelineCtx: group_filter: Option<Arc<GroupFilter>>  (or borrow; check lifetime constraints)
2. In run_pipeline(), in the group loop (currently lines ~390-426), add before GroupName::new(): if let Some(ref filter) = ctx.group_filter { if !filter.accepts(group_name_str) { tracing::debug!(group = %group_name_str, "skipped: not matched by group filter"); continue; } }
3. In crates/transit/src/main.rs startup code: after Config::validate() succeeds, call GroupFilter::new(&config.groups.names).expect("config already validated") to build filter; wrap in Arc; pass to PipelineCtx in all run_pipeline() call sites
4. If config.groups.names is empty: GroupFilter::new would return Err — but Config::validate() already rejects empty names (so this expect is safe; add comment explaining why)
5. Update any test helpers that construct PipelineCtx to pass group_filter: None (no filter = accept all groups, preserving existing test behavior)

## Defensive programming rules
- group_filter: None means accept all groups (backward-compatible default for tests)
- Never panic in the hot path; the filter is pre-validated at startup
- Log filtered groups at debug level only, never info (high volume)
- If all groups of an article are filtered, the article's IPFS block is still stored — only log entries are skipped
- No unwrap() in the pipeline code path; use expect() only where invariant is documented

## Agent team
Standard: Agent R (read pipeline.rs PipelineCtx + run_pipeline(), main.rs startup), Agent I (implement above algorithm), Agent V (cargo test --workspace + clippy)

## Tests
Tests are in whss.7 (integration). whss.5 just needs cargo test --workspace to pass clean.
